salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with casual loading of 25% added before super.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied when converting hourly to annual?
faqs.a: Casual loading of 25% is added on top of the base hourly rate. For example, if the base rate is $26.44 (National Minimum Wage), the casual rate becomes $33.05. When converting to annual, use the casual rate: $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80. Super is then calculated at 12% on that amount, paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor: $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. Award rates are higher minimums set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries and occupations. Most employees are covered by an award, which may include higher base rates, penalty rates, and allowances. Always check the relevant award via the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross salary. It is not deducted from your pay. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830, meaning super stops accruing once your earnings exceed that amount. For example, on a $65,000 annual salary, super adds $7,800 per year to your retirement savings.

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: A Practical Guide

Whether you're negotiating a salary offer or checking your pay as a casual worker, converting your hourly rate to an annual figure is a fundamental skill. This guide uses the latest figures from the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Taxation Office to help you understand the numbers – including casual loading, super paid on top, and how even the **Jim Chalmers salary** fits into the same tax and super system.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks.

We assume a standard full-time week of 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Act. If you work part-time or irregular hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. For example:

- National Minimum Wage (from 1 July 2026): $26.44/hour × 38 × 52 = **$52,254.88 per year**.
- Casual rate (including 25% loading): $33.05/hour × 38 × 52 = **$65,306.80 per year**.

Remember: the formula assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. It's a starting point, not a final pay slip.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor: $26.44 per hour ($33.05 for casuals). Most employees are covered by an award – a legal document that sets minimum pay rates, penalties, and allowances. Award rates are generally higher than the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75%, so check your specific award using the [pay guides](/blog) on this site.

### Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

Casual employees receive a 25% loading to compensate for lack of paid leave. When using our [the timesheet](/), enter your base hourly rate. The checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top – never enter a rate that already includes loading.

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross salary. It does not reduce your take-home pay. For the 2026–27 year, the maximum contribution base is $270,830. So on a $65,306.80 casual salary, super adds $7,836.82 per year.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Using the 2026–27 resident tax scale:
- Nil tax on first $18,200
- 15% on $18,201–$45,000
- 30% on $45,001–$135,000
- 37% on $135,001–$190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Plus Medicare levy of 2% (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 not confirmed).

For a full-time worker on $65,306.80 (casual rate), tax would be approximately $11,547 plus Medicare $1,306, leaving about $52,454 take-home. Super adds $7,836 on top.

### The Jim Chalmers Salary in Context

The Treasurer's salary is set by the Remuneration Tribunal and is well above the average. But even the **Jim Chalmers salary** – like all salaries – is subject to the same super guarantee cap and progressive tax scales. While most workers earn far less, understanding the conversion from hourly to annual helps everyone see where they stand relative to the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and the broader economy.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Breakdown

If you're paid fortnightly, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the National Minimum Wage:
- Weekly: $1,004.90
- Fortnightly: $2,009.80
- Casual weekly: $1,255.90
- Casual fortnightly: $2,511.80

These figures exclude super, which is paid on top.

### Using This Site

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool lets you enter your base rate and toggle casual loading. The result shows annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. For more detail on award rates, see the [reference tables](/data).

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
